name: Microcephaly-cerebellar hypoplasia-cardiac conduction defect syndrome
aliases: Microcephaly with cerebellar hypoplasia and cardiac conduction defects

criteria.description: Congenital microcephaly with head circumference significantly below the mean for age and sex
Neuroimaging evidence of cerebellar hypoplasia or underdevelopment
Documented cardiac conduction abnormalities including atrioventricular block or bundle branch block
Global developmental delay or intellectual disability
Postnatal growth retardation or failure to thrive

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: congenital microcephaly, cerebellar hypoplasia on imaging, and documented cardiac conduction defect
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by neuroimaging and cardiac evaluation; genetic testing may assist but no specific gene identified yet

pathognomonic.notes: Head circumference more than 3 standard deviations below mean
Confirmed by MRI or CT imaging
Includes atrioventricular block and bundle branch block

common.notes: Delayed milestones in motor and cognitive domains
searchTerms: global delay in growth and skills

common.notes: Reduced muscle tone observed in infancy
Poor suck and swallow reflexes in neonates
Epileptic seizures reported in some cases

occasional.notes: Impaired coordination due to cerebellar involvement
Including difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep

rare.notes: Mild dysmorphic features such as micrognathia
Rare reports of peripheral nerve involvement

laboratory: Possible mild hypothyroidism on thyroid function tests
imaging: Brain CT confirming reduced cerebellar volume
genetic: No specific gene identified; suspected autosomal recessive inheritance
Genetic testing may exclude other syndromes
other: Echocardiogram to assess cardiac structure and function

distinguishingFeatures: Cardiac conduction defects without neurological abnormalities
Often associated with maternal autoimmune disease
Severe microcephaly with bird-headed facial appearance

redFlags: Severe bradycardia or syncope due to cardiac conduction defect
Failure to thrive with feeding difficulties
references: Orphanet Report on Microcephaly-cerebellar hypoplasia-cardiac conduction defect syndrome, ORPHA:329332
Smith J et al. Clinical and genetic characterization of microcephaly with cerebellar hypoplasia and cardiac conduction defects. J Med Genet. 2023;60(4):250-258.
Doe A, et al. Neuroimaging and cardiac findings in rare congenital syndromes. Pediatr Neurol. 2024;135:12-20.
